reviewer: adversarial finder (score not authoritative; see PROMPT-STANDARD "How to review a prompt")

gaps.property: Module-spec rule 7 (dependencies and their real APIs) / property 2
gaps.problem: Every dependency access path in §7 has one `.api` too many. `src/core/registry.js:36` passes `modules: this.apis` and `register()` sets `this.apis[name] = def.api`, so `ctx.modules.terrain` IS the api object — `ctx.modules.terrain.api.getHeight` is undefined. The module's own existing code already does it correctly (`index.js:187` `ctx.modules.environment?.setupMaterial?.(S.mat)`). Two consequences are not cosmetic: (a) §7 says `setupMaterial(material)` **must** be called or CSM shadows and fog are not injected — written as `ctx.modules.environment.api.setupMaterial(...)` it throws, and written defensively with `?.` it silently no-ops, killing items 1, 9, 15 and the whole §8 golden-hour read with no error in the log; (b) item 7's placeholder-fence flag is gated on `ctx.modules.props?.api?.rebuild` existing, which is permanently undefined, so the placeholder boundary is always on and `--showcase all` gets exactly the doubled, z-fighting lot boundary that item 7 and §6 exist to prevent — and it is invisible in `?showcase=buildings`.
gaps.fix: Strike `.api` from all five paragraphs: `ctx.modules.terrain`, `ctx.modules.roads`, `ctx.modules.zoning`, `ctx.modules.environment`, `ctx.modules.simulation`. Change item 7's gate to `ctx.modules.props?.rebuild`. Add one line to §7: 'ctx.modules.<name> IS that module's api object (registry.js passes `modules: this.apis`); there is no `.api` wrapper.'

gaps.property: Property 5 (bounded blast radius) — ownership conflict with another module's spec
gaps.problem: `docs/prompts/modules/props.md` lines 37-39 instructs the props builder in the opposite direction: '`buildings` already generates its own lot hedge and lot fence (`generate.js`: `p.hedge`, `p.fence`). To avoid doubled boundaries in `?showcase=all`, props places `fence`/`hedge` **only** on lots with `lot.buildingId == null`.' buildings.md item 7 forbids buildings from emitting any boundary and asserts props already fences every residential lot. Both true today (buildings/generate.js:75-76, 867-880 emits them; props/place.js:334 fences unconditionally), but if both builders comply with their own spec the occupied residential lots end up with **no** boundary at all — contradicting this spec's own §3 target ('Every lot is bounded: clipped hedge, timber fence or a low wall') and losing a whole-game round to a regression neither critic can attribute.
gaps.fix: Do not settle a two-module handover inside one module's spec. Either (a) edit props.md in the same commit to delete the `lot.buildingId == null` condition and state that props fences every residential lot regardless of occupancy, consuming `buildings.lotSurface(id)`; or (b) keep boundaries with buildings and delete item 7's prohibition. Whichever is chosen, state it once in ARCHITECTURE §15 as the ownership line and have both specs point at it.

gaps.property: Property 2 (falsifiable) / property 3 (numeric) — items that are opinions in checklist clothing
gaps.problem: Four graded items have no mechanical fail condition, and each is a guaranteed round of argument. Item 5: 'an art director can name the type of every building from silhouette + material alone' — unfalsifiable as written; the accompanying probe only proves 40 byClass keys exist. Item 10: the entire tiling test ('no facade shows an identical bay pattern repeating more than 4 times horizontally', 'no two towers in the frame wear the same facade') has no counting rule, no crop, no probe. Item 3: '≥ 3 emissive brightness tiers' and 'both a warm (r>g>b) and a cool (b≥r) tint present on the same facade' name no measurement method, and 'median luminance of lit-window pixels ≥ 6× median luminance of the unlit facade' gives no rule for segmenting window pixels from facade pixels. Item 1: 'window openings recessed ≥ 0.10 m behind the wall plane' cannot be measured in a PNG at all (the tris0/building probe backstops the presence of relief, not the depth).
gaps.fix: Give each a probe field, since §2 already establishes the pattern. Item 5: replace the art-director sentence with `styleCounts().byClass` plus a required `features().materialByClass` showing ≥ 4 distinct facade material ids and ≥ 4 distinct crown keys across the 8 type/density classes. Item 10: `styleCounts().byStyleId` — no `styleId` used by more than N buildings in the `skyline` selection — plus a stated maximum run length exposed as `features().maxBayRun`. Item 3: define tiers as distinct values of the baked brightness attribute (`features().litTiers >= 3`) and warm/cool as counts of baked tint values; define the 6× ratio over a named 200×200 crop with the lit set = pixels whose baked emissive attribute is on. Item 1: move the 0.10/0.04/0.15 m depths into a `features().reliefDepths` probe read from the generated geometry, and keep the screenshot for the shadow.

gaps.problem: `$REF` is hard-coded to `/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-SimBuild/c06ed41b-9bdf-5ab7-ace6-40b62a5e4281/scratchpad/ref` — a session-scoped scratchpad UUID. A builder or critic in any other session has no such directory, and items 3, 4 and 13 plus all of §3 then reference images that do not exist, with no instruction for what to do. props.md has already solved this (line 9: resolve `$SIMBUILD_REF`, else the repo copy, and 'the CS2-LOOK.md descriptions are the normative statement of each anchor and the round proceeds against those — a missing $REF is never a reason to stop, to ask, or to skip an item'). The images also exist in-repo at `docs/reference/cs2_1.jpg … cs2_8.jpg`.
gaps.fix: Replace the `$REF` line with props.md's resolution-order paragraph verbatim, pointing at `docs/reference/` as the second resolution step and naming `docs/reference/CS2-LOOK.md` as the normative fallback.

gaps.property: Property 1 (sequenced) / property 2 — spec is self-inconsistent by its own rule
gaps.problem: Item 17 grades 'triangles ≤ 1_400_000 at `aerial` and `overview`', but none of the seven commands in §4 shoots the `overview` camera. §4 states its own rule: 'A criterion that names a shot not produced above is a bug in this spec, not a licence to invent one.' The critic must therefore either skip a budget clause or invent a shot, and the builder cannot know which.
gaps.fix: Either add `--cameras overview --times 12` to the §4 command block, or delete `and overview` from item 17 and from the §5 budget table row.

gaps.property: Property 3 (numeric) — a requirement satisfiable two ways
gaps.problem: Item 5 says levels within a class must differ in floors, 'strictly non-decreasing with level, ≥ +1 floor per step for high density'. 'Strictly' and 'non-decreasing' contradict each other, and the only quantified step applies to high density — so a builder can ship low-density levels 1 through 5 with identical floor counts and be fully compliant with the letter of the item while failing its intent (growth reads as growth). Item 23 has the same shape: ≥ +2.5 m per step is specified for high density only.
gaps.fix: Rewrite as: 'floors are non-decreasing with level and strictly increase at least twice across levels 1→5 in every class; high density gains ≥ 1 floor at every step, low density gains ≥ 1 floor at ≥ 2 of the 4 steps and otherwise differs in footprint, crown or material.' Mirror the low-density clause in item 23.

gaps.property: Property 3 (numeric) — stated facts about the tree that are wrong
gaps.problem: Item 17 and the §5 table say the declared budget 'stays `{ drawCalls: 400, triangles: 2_000_000 }`', but `src/modules/buildings/index.js:175` currently declares `{ drawCalls: 320, triangles: 2_500_000 }`. A builder who reads 'stays' will not edit it and will fail item 17 on a one-line omission. Separately, §7 states props declares `budget {drawCalls: 400, triangles: 2_200_000}`; the real value in `src/modules/props/index.js:144` is `triangles: 1_900_000`.
gaps.fix: Change 'stays' to 'must be changed to' and note the current 320 / 2.5 M values explicitly. Correct the props triangle figure to 1_900_000, or drop the figure — it does nothing for this module.

gaps.property: Property 3 (numeric) — a governing cap derived from an unmeasured number
gaps.problem: §5 derives the `stats().draws ≤ 285` cap as '400 scene − ~115 neighbours (terrain ~20, roads ~80, zoning overlay plus environment ~15)'. Those are ARCHITECTURE §9's demo-city allotments, not measurements of `?showcase=buildings`. The existing shots for this showcase (`shots/buildings/dev_aerial_12.json`, `dev2_closeup_12.json`) show 158 and 128 draw calls for the *whole* scene including buildings, so the neighbours are nowhere near 115. The cap is safe in the conservative direction, but it is presented as arithmetic and a builder who trusts it will mis-plan its chunk/batch budget by a factor of two.
gaps.fix: Replace '~115' with the measured neighbour figure: state 'measured at `?showcase=buildings` with the module staged empty, neighbours are ≤ 40 draws; the 285 cap therefore leaves headroom for democity, where §9 allots buildings 500 of 1500.' Or drop the derivation and simply assert the cap.

gaps.property: Role-prompt rule (invariants live in the role file, not sixteen module specs)
gaps.problem: The §4 preamble — the gauntlet-does-not-shoot-presets fact and the seven-command shot block — is invariant tooling behaviour, not something specific to buildings. It also contradicts ARCHITECTURE §8 ('plus the module's own presets') and CRITIC.md's own shooting recipe ('gauntlet --times 12,22 ... Plus every preset the module declares'). Duplicated per module, this is exactly the drift the standard forbids: a fix to gauntlet.mjs would leave sixteen specs lying.
gaps.fix: Move the tool behaviour and the preset-shooting recipe into CRITIC.md and BUILDER.md, fix ARCHITECTURE §8's stale sentence, and leave in buildings.md only the module-specific part: the extra `--cameras`/`--times` combinations this module's criteria need.

gaps.property: Property 2 (falsifiable) — pass criteria that do not execute or are undefined at an edge
gaps.problem: Item 3's literal criterion is `grep -n "fract(sin(" src/modules/buildings/` — without `-r` this errors with 'Is a directory' rather than returning nothing, so the pass condition as written can never be met (items 7 and 20 correctly use `grep -rn`). Separately, `groundFloorDistinct` in §2 is 'the ground storey is ≥ 4.5 m tall while every storey above it is 2.9–4.1 m' — undefined for a single-storey building, where the second clause is vacuous; since item 4 requires ≥ 0.80 of all commercial-or-mixed items in the selection to satisfy it, whether one-storey shops count as passing or failing can swing that ratio.
gaps.fix: Add `-r` to item 3's grep. Add to the `groundFloorDistinct` predicate: 'a building with a single storey satisfies this if that storey is ≥ 4.5 m; buildings with floors < 2 are excluded from item 4's denominator.'

gaps.property: Property 3 (numeric) — a constraint stricter than it reads
gaps.problem: Item 6 requires `features().clutterTwins === 0` over the whole showcase, i.e. no two flat-roofed buildings whose centres are within 45 m carry an identical roof-clutter multiset. In the `catalog` block — 40 buildings laid out one per cell on a flat grid — every neighbour pair is likely within 45 m, so all flat-roofed catalog entries must carry globally distinct clutter multisets on top of their other required differences. That is satisfiable (seed clutter from building id) but it is a trap a builder will hit late, after the catalog grid is built, and it is not flagged anywhere.
gaps.fix: Either state the catalog cell pitch as > 45 m in §8, or exempt the catalog selection from `clutterTwins` and evaluate item 6's twin test on the downtown/suburb selections only — with the exemption written into the §2 predicate so builder and critic compute the same number.

strengths: Property 3 (numeric) is exceptionally well served: nearly every ratio in §4 has both numerator and denominator defined as a named probe field, and §2 fixes the predicate for each one (`clutterTwins`, `adjacentTwins`, `nonRect`, `groundFloorDistinct`, `balconied`, `litCells`) so builder and critic compute the same integer rather than argue about a word. The selection-by-(x,z,r) mechanism, anchored to `presets['<name>'].target`, is a genuinely good invention: it makes 'downtown' and 'at the closeup' mechanically defined in world space instead of by eye.
The world-data block in §2 is copied verbatim from ARCHITECTURE §3 (items map, version, spawn/demolish/levelUp/at) and the `buildings:changed` payload matches §5 exactly. No paraphrase drift.

Factual claims about the tree are unusually accurate where I checked them: `world.zones` lot fields (`nx, nz, ax, az, corner, t, buildingId`) match `zoning/grid.js` line 377-388 exactly; the 15 existing `api` members in `src/modules/buildings/index.js` match the '14 already exist plus stats' claim; `props/place.js placeGardens()` really does fence every residential lot; `docs/STATUS.json` really does still list props as stub/round 0; the six declared preset names match `showcase.js CAMERAS`.

The claim that `tools/gauntlet.mjs` never shoots a module's declared presets is true of the actual tool (it iterates only `--cameras`), contradicting the stale ARCHITECTURE §8 — and the spec supplies the exact command set that produces every shot name it later cites. I verified the filename convention (`${cam}_${time.replace('.','p')}`) and every named shot except `overview` is produced by those commands.

§6 failure modes are real, not generic: the per-pixel window static is `environment_r2.md` issue 2 and `src/modules/buildings/material.js:39` genuinely carries the same `fract(sin(dot(...)))` fed from an interpolated varying; 'uniform interior glow' matches the literal `+= ... * 0.03` term two lines below it; specular sparkle is `roads_r1` issue 5; washed-out noon is `roads_r1` issue 4.

Correct division of labour with the role files: blast radius, anti-inflation, autonomy, liveness and resumability are left to BUILDER.md/CRITIC.md and not restated, exactly as the standard's role-prompt rule requires.

The three-way draw-call disambiguation (declared budget vs scene `.json` figure vs `stats().draws`) pre-empts a whole class of builder/critic argument, and the caps are consistent with ARCHITECTURE §9 (400 of the 500 allotted).
verdict: 8.0 — fail (pass is 8.5). This is a genuinely strong spec and one of the better ones in the repo: the §2 probe API with fixed predicates and named denominators turns most of the 23 acceptance items into arithmetic, the world-data block is copied verbatim from ARCHITECTURE §3, the failure modes are traceable to real critic reports and to the exact lines of the current code, the budget is consistent with §9 and three-way disambiguated, and it correctly leaves BUILDER/CRITIC invariants alone. It falls short on two systemic faults and one cluster of soft items. (1) Every dependency path in §7 carries a `.api` that does not exist — `ctx.modules.<name>` IS the api object per registry.js:36 — which makes the mandatory `setupMaterial` call a silent no-op and, worse, permanently arms item 7's placeholder-fence flag, producing the exact doubled-boundary failure the item was written to prevent, invisibly, in `--showcase all`. (2) Item 7 settles a two-module ownership handover unilaterally, and props.md states the opposite rule; both builders complying leaves occupied residential lots with no boundary at all, contradicting this spec's own §3 target. On top of that, items 5, 10, 3 and 1 contain claims a critic cannot mechanically fail ('an art director can name the type', 'no two towers wear the same facade', '≥ 3 brightness tiers', '0.10 m recess in a PNG'), item 17 grades an `overview` shot the §4 command block never produces, item 5's 'strictly non-decreasing' is self-contradictory and leaves low-density growth unconstrained, and the declared-budget line says 'stays' about values index.js does not currently hold. None of these is fatal; all are cheap to fix, and with the `.api` correction, the props ownership decision moved to ARCHITECTURE §15, the four soft items given probe fields, and the `overview`/`$REF` inconsistencies closed, this is a 9.
